gold.question: Goods sold under Directive (EU) 2019/771 are not in conformity. May the consumer choose between repair and replacement, and must that remedy be free of charge?
gold.reference_answer: The consumer may choose repair or replacement in order to have the goods brought into conformity, unless the chosen remedy is impossible or would impose disproportionate costs on the seller in the circumstances listed in Article 13(2). Where repair or replacement is used, it must be carried out free of charge, within a reasonable time after the seller is informed, and without significant inconvenience to the consumer.
key_facts: 2. In order to have the goods brought into conformity, the consumer may choose between repair and replacement, unless the remedy chosen would be impossible or, compared to the other remedy, would impose costs on the seller that would be disproportionate, taking into account all circumstances, including:

1. Repairs or replacements shall be carried out:
(a) free of charge;

(b) within a reasonable period of time from the moment the seller has been informed by the consumer about the lack of conformity; and
(c) without any significant inconvenience to the consumer, taking into account the nature of the goods and the purpose for which the consumer required the goods.
